title: Welcome to MOSCATELLI Atlas
summary: What Atlas is for, what belongs here and how to distinguish institutional knowledge from live operational work.
contentNotice: Demonstration content for Atlas interface development; not final MOSCATELLI policy.

blocks.text: Atlas is the reference layer: it explains standards, procedures and institutional knowledge. MainHub remains the place for live operational work, current projects and records.

blocks.label: Working distinction
blocks.text: If the information should still be useful after the current task has ended, it probably belongs in Atlas. If it represents live work, ownership or a current operational record, it belongs in MainHub.
Atlas should contain durable guidance that another team member can rely upon without reconstructing context from messages, meetings or memory.

items: Standards that define an expected quality threshold
Procedures that should be repeated consistently
Reference material that explains MOSCATELLI terminology or decisions
Learning material that supports onboarding and role development

steps.title: Confirm the status
steps.text: Check whether the article is current, under review, superseded or archived.

steps.title: Read the governing context
steps.text: Use the owner, approver and review dates to understand who maintains the reference.

steps.title: Follow related material
steps.text: Move to a linked procedure or MainHub destination when the reference points to live work.

blocks.text: Demonstration content in this preview is explicitly labelled and should not be treated as final company policy.

The long-term purpose of Atlas is to reduce dependency on individual memory. A useful knowledge system makes the company easier to operate, teach and improve without making the work feel bureaucratic.
